purpose: the access lift is the only entrance of the hideout from the surface; workers and slaves ride it down with cargo, it also stores construction equipment.
what: a heavy freight elevator inside an octagonal shaft room: in the middle a large square red steel lift platform (the lift car seen from above, its roof a dark square grated hatch in a thick red frame with warning lamps at the corners), around it four grey L-shaped concrete loading ramps and guard rails, bare floor between them, a couple of tool crates by the wall

purpose: the hangar holds one aircraft: the craft lands here from above through the open roof and stands on the landing pad, ground crew refuel, maintain and repair it.
what: one huge open landing bay with nothing in the middle but the pad (no inner walls, the whole square is one open floor): a scuffed red painted floor with darker red camouflage patches, a big round golden-brass landing pad with a sword emblem and four arrow markings pointing to its centre, yellow-black hazard stripes and a vent grille in the top right corner, fuel hoses, tool carts and spare-part crates only along the outer walls

purpose: crew quarters where 35 pirates live, eat, sleep, heal their wounds and kill boredom.
what: crew quarters: small bunk cabins behind low white partitions along the walls with white beds and pink blankets, lockers, an orange mesh floor walkway in the middle with a grey mess table

purpose: a stylish but drafty cave dwelling dug in the earth for 15 people and 10 tamed animals, also used as a storeroom.
what: a crude dug-out burrow, primitive and handmade, with no machines, no metal boxes and no electronics anywhere: a packed brown earth floor with roots and pebbles, dark earth walls; in the middle a small ring of stones with a glowing campfire and embers; sleeping hollows lined with straw and old patched blankets along the walls and in the corners, a straw nest with animal bedding for tamed beasts, burlap sacks, wooden crates, clay jars and a few bundles

purpose: a security corridor: a simple 4-way passage with a central chamber that links parts of the hideout to the pipes and the power grid; the sewers below are grated off; one security camera.
what: a cross-shaped corridor junction: a brown and orange checkered steel grate floor, pipes and power cables along the walls, one small security camera

purpose: an Old Earth science lab, an ancient treasure, where up to 12 scientists invent, study old technology and interrogate prisoners.
what: a research laboratory: a pale pinkish tiled floor, long white L-shaped workbenches with lab glassware, microscopes and a few old computer screens

purpose: a real workshop with modern machine tools where 30 workers build laser guns and other equipment by hand.
what: an engineering workshop on a grey concrete floor: heavy machine tools and presses, a lamp and a crane hook at the top, a striped conveyor belt along the bottom, parts bins

purpose: the vaults: all guns, munitions, treasure and assorted junk of the hideout are stored here.
what: a storeroom on a grey concrete floor divided by white low walls: stacked orange crates, grey sacks and bundles, a small purple cart, a potted green plant in the corner

purpose: a hi-res radar station that watches the sky for prey within 1600 miles.
what: a small radar station: an octagonal room with a deep violet floor, a white radar antenna mast and dish in the middle, cables snaking across the floor

purpose: a battery of heavy laser cannons that shoots at enemy ships, with a defensive laser turret in case enemies get inside.
what: a laser defense battery in a cross-shaped room: a white spherical laser turret with a red-and-white striped barrel pointing up, on a dark violet four-pointed mount

purpose: a sickbay where nurses heal the wounded crew faster.
what: a medical bay: a green padded medical floor in two sections with a large white cross in a red circle painted in the middle, clean and bright

purpose: a large prison for 100 prisoners with remote locks and electronic detection, and a guard tower with a small cannon.
what: a crowded prison block packed with barred cells, no empty floor: a grey steel grate floor; a row of five small barred cells with dark red bunks along the left wall and another row along the right wall; in the middle a freestanding block of ten barred cells in two columns back to back, each cell with a dark red bunk; narrow grey walkways between the rows of cells; a small guard post with a green lamp and a little cannon in the bottom right corner

purpose: a dojo: a dangerous training course with a shooting range whose targets shoot back, a boxing ring, weights and an arcade corner.
what: a dojo: an orange rubber mesh floor, two grey tiled shooting-range lanes on the left with yellow lamps at the far end, a blue punching ball and weights

purpose: an onsen: a hot spring of hot, healthy, glowing water, the hideout's healing spa and cultural centre, filled with mind-liberating weed fumes.
what: a hot-spring bath built into the rock: a pool of glowing blue water on the right, thick white steam clouds over the left half, an orange tiled rim

purpose: an arcane chamber for magic rites and summoning.
what: an occult summoning chamber with no machines and no electronics: a dark blood-red stone floor; in the middle a large eight-pointed rune circle deeply carved into the floor, its lines glowing bright orange-red like embers, filling most of the room; black candles with small flames on its eight points; a carved orange stone border; a few stone pedestals, ritual bowls and old bones by the walls

purpose: a large plant that refines hellerium: extractor, still, refinery and power plant in one, worked by 75 workers.
what: a hellerium processing plant, one large open hall (no inner walls) on a dark grey floor: three tall violet-grey cylindrical tanks on the left, a round pool of bubbling glowing green hellerium in the middle, pink pipes, a control console at the bottom, orange lamps in the top corners, a blue sign at the bottom right

purpose: an overcharged radar station that scans the sky far beyond a normal radar and can also jam the navigation of enemy craft that try to land near the hideout; technicians keep the dish running.
what: a large radar station: a dark slate-blue steel floor in a square room, in the middle a big four-armed radar dish array with pale grey-brown curved reflector panels radiating from a small central hub with a blue-yellow indicator light, cables and a few bolts on the floor between the arms, nothing else

purpose: a repulsor beam emitter that slows hostile craft trying to land near the hideout so that all defence batteries get to fire twice; it is powered from the fusion furnace and tended by a few technicians.
what: an octagonal emitter room: an orange-tan metal plate floor laid out as a regular grid of square panels, grey-lilac round emitter nodes with small orange-red indicator dots at the grid intersections, a worn lilac rim along the octagonal edge, nothing in the way of the grid

purpose: a large cave where the pirates keep up to thirty beasts and store supplies; the animals are used for various fun and games.
what: a rough natural cave pen: a dark brown earth and rock floor, a heap of golden-tan straw bedding and a pile of bones or hay bundles in the middle, a couple of small red scraps and tufts of green grass at the bottom, dark rocky walls, no machines

purpose: a larger and more efficient version of the crew quarters, built from junkyard parts with extra creature comforts, housing a great crowd of pirates who eat, sleep and recover here, with a small storage corner.
what: one large open hall of crew quarters (no inner walls except low light-lilac partitions): orange striped mesh floor walkways forming a cross in the middle, around them in a 4x4 pattern small bunk cubicles behind low pale-lilac partitions, each with a bed with a pink-and-brown blanket and a small green plant or locker at its corner, a couple of dark round floor hatches in the walkways, thin cables along the top

purpose: a sealed luxury condo for the hideout's elite, inspired by guild executive suites: spacious apartments with their own training corner, a pool garden and a defending laser cannon.
what: one large open hall (no inner walls, only low white partitions): a pale grey tiled floor, a long rectangular blue-water pool in the middle running top to bottom with an orange tiled rim and rows of green hedges on both sides, apartments with white beds and brown sofas along the left and right edges, a laser cannon turret and machinery blocks at the top right, a red armchair at the bottom right and a round blue sofa at the bottom left, a pink-and-white striped bed corner at the top left

purpose: a ruined armoured defence bunker, heavily shot up: the concrete is cracked and pitted, the guns inside are silent and the garrison is gone.
what: a shell-shattered bunker roof seen from above: a light grey cracked concrete slab covering the whole room, many dark round bullet craters and blast holes with dark rims and a few small gouges scattered unevenly over it, dust and rubble, no intact equipment

purpose: the headquarters of the revolution, a fortified barracks with a command post and training yard, now heavily damaged by a long siege and bombardment.
what: one huge open ruined compound (no inner walls): a grey armoured concrete outer ring with a torn red flag and a faded emblem at the top left, a rubble-strewn dirt-brown inner yard with a lighter grey paved square in the middle holding a few blue crates and a small green plant, large dark blast craters and many small scorched holes scattered everywhere, a broken fence bottom left with a metal grate hatch, no intact machinery

purpose: an optimised and robotised storage complex that is practically bottomless; the hideout keeps its guns, ammunition, treasure and junk here and a crew of workers sorts the cargo.
what: one huge open warehouse hall (no outer-room walls inside, only low white-edged shelf bays): a grey concrete floor with painted diamond markers and orange direction arrows, at the top rows of violet-grey crates, stacks of orange-brown barrels and long orange pallets along the right edge, at the right and bottom shelf bays holding red drums, dark machine parts and violet crates, middle bays with orange and brown stacked sacks, green hedge-like bundles standing in short rows, a small guard booth with a blue item in the top-left corner, two dark robot loaders at the left, a green shrub line on the left edge

purpose: a prison block for twice the prisoners, with electronic surveillance, better restraints and a professional guard force; captured enemies are held here.
what: a prison block: a dark grey steel floor with a central lighter grey corridor running top to bottom with small red warning lights, on both sides rows of small cells with dark red-maroon bunks behind grey bars, two guard posts with a blue-and-white desk at the top left and bottom right corners

purpose: a chamber where brainers bond with the gestalt consciousness of the alenium crystal to sharpen their minds and extend their senses; the glowing crystal is dangerously addictive.
what: an octagonal chamber: a deep glowing blue floor with lighter blue ripples, two grey-white conical crystal pedestals with swirling shiny surfaces at the left and right, a small orange lamp on a thin pole at the top left, thin cables along the floor, a worn orange-gold rim around the octagon

purpose: a tactical command centre where officers plan raids and track the field; here it lies in ruins, burnt out and unusable.
what: a ruined command room: a rusty dark brown floor with scorched patches, a central dull dark console slab with a pale oval panel in the middle, round dark blast holes with orange rims at the top left, bottom left and right, broken pipes and wires along the edges, no intact screens

purpose: an anti-aircraft flak tower in disrepair: its guns are wrecked and it barely shoots at enemy ships anymore.
what: a battered octagonal gun platform: a pinkish-grey stone floor with dark brown scorch marks and several round black blast holes with orange rims, a small bright green lamp or plant on the top, a cracked dark red-brown rim around the octagon, no intact gun

purpose: a railgun battery with high firepower but heavy upkeep; it shoots at enemy ships and also has a turret to defend the hideout against ground assault.
what: a railgun battery in a cross-shaped room: a warm brown-orange floor in a plus shape, in the middle a dark grey spherical turret base with two tall black railgun barrels pointing up, a dark four-pointed star mount under it with pale steel highlights

purpose: a huge spa complex with a swimming pool, fighting ring, games terrace, arcade room and sauna; the crew trains, relaxes and recovers here, and the less clothing the better.
what: one large open hall (no inner walls): an orange rubber mesh floor, a big square pool of bright blue water with a white rim in the middle and a raised terraced edge around it, two small grey pool-side steps at its bottom, striped blue-and-white deck chairs on the left, a green cactus-like plant on the right, a blue sphere ball at the top left, a grey diving-board or machine block at the top, a red carpet square at the bottom right and a smaller red mat at the bottom left

purpose: a pleasure den where rich and powerful guests are lured to gamble, drink and be persuaded to support the cause; it earns money and doubles as a mess hall.
what: a dark pleasure parlour: a black grated floor in a central aisle with a green round table and little yellow chips on it, purple-violet couches with golden cushions along the left and right walls, an amber-gold framed archway at the top and bottom, a dark red carpet corner at the top right, thin brass-gold partitions

purpose: a clinic where eager staff treat the crew while they eat great food; recovery is miraculous, and some come even when healthy.
what: a clinic room: a plum-purple padded floor split into two soft sections by a darker seam across the middle, a white circle with a red cross painted in the top centre, a worn pink-purple texture, clean and soft

purpose: a defensive room with spike traps built into the floor to slow down invaders; the spikes do not tell friend from foe.
what: a square trap room: a dusty brown-grey stone floor with five round dark red pressure plates with black centres, one in each corner area and one in the middle in a dice-five pattern, pale cracks, nothing else

purpose: a weed plantation where the crew grows crops of weed in hydroponic beds under lamps and watering pipes.
what: one large open hall (no inner walls): long parallel rows of dark brown planting beds with rows of green sprouts in four groups, a big lilac-grey cross-shaped pipe running through the middle both horizontally and vertically with four round bolted junction valves, a grey concrete rim around the room

purpose: an empty body farm: a cloning vat hall where bodies are grown, now with all the tanks drained and ready for new batches.
what: one large open hall (no inner walls): a dusty pinkish-grey checkered floor, a regular 4x4 grid of upright round blue-glass vats with lilac metal rims and pale blue glowing tops (all empty), thin white pipes running between the vats, a small pale blue and white mesh service area in the bottom-left corner with green lights, blue clamps in the top corners

purpose: a mint with presses and plates for printing counterfeit money; runts work the machines day and night.
what: a small print shop: a dark red floor with scattered yellow rivets, a big dark grey banknote printing press in the upper middle, a conveyor with rows of small red and dark rollers along the bottom, black frame walls

purpose: a workshop-type facility with a hundred workers that builds items with very intricate internal structure, such as advanced armour suits.
what: one large open hall (no inner walls) on a dark grey floor covered with rows of round bolt hatches: two printer tracks on the left half and one on the right with orange-brown long machine gantries with small coloured lamps, small violet-grey parts and stamped grey plates scattered between, orange hoists in the top corners, a pale pipe along the left side

purpose: private study labs where brainers meditate and do serious research away from the main lab.
what: a study lab split into two narrow halves by a thin wall: a pale pinkish-grey tiled floor, in each half a tall white curled glass tube or still with bent pipes and a base, grey-lilac equipment racks, quiet and clean

purpose: an analytics room with the best media equipment, where brainers brainstorm and argue violently.
what: a study room: a pale pinkish tiled floor, in the middle three pairs of small white-lilac desks with screens in two rows of three, a long grey console or whiteboard along the top, a small door-like panel on the left wall, a plain pale rim

purpose: an arcane facility where brainers study the secrets of the universe from an upper chamber and adepts train their voodoo in a lower hall, tuned to detect distant enemy hideouts.
what: an octagonal arcane chamber: a deep violet-purple floor with a faint glowing ring pattern, in the middle a red-pink pulsing orb, four smaller violet orbs at the corners joined by thin glowing lines, worn orange-gold rim around the octagon

purpose: the red mage's improved tower: a dark sorcerous fortress with a mainframe, biotech, surgery and power plant, home to brainers, hiding the hideout from sight and lashing out with mind bolts.
what: an occult tower room: a black floor with a big ring of pale grey-white rounded pods or skulls in the centre circle, a red pentagram star with a bright red centre in the middle, tiny blue sparks and orange-gold glints, darker corners, a thick brass-gold-edged black border

purpose: a missile silo holding nuclear missiles that launch against enemy ships attacking the hideout; crews keep the rockets fuelled and armed and fire them from here when unwelcome guests appear overhead.
what: an octagonal missile silo room with a dark slate-purple floor with a faint diagonal hatch pattern: a long dark steel silo hatch running diagonally from the upper left towards the bottom, with a small red warning lamp in the middle, yellow-black hazard stripes along the upper left, bottom and right edges, a few cables and pipes by the walls

purpose: a battery of cloaking devices of the kind mounted on the crew's ships; it hides the whole hideout from enemy eyes and makes it much harder to spot.
what: an octagonal technical room with a violet-purple floor: four large round brown-grey domed cloaking generators arranged in a two-by-two grid with a gap between them, small orange lamps and short orange cables in the gaps and near the walls

purpose: a small cheap outpost: a few bunks and a little storage for a backwater hideout, with a modest radar to watch the surroundings and a corner for the crew to rest.
what: a small compact outpost room with a warm orange and brown diagonally striped mesh floor: in the middle a single grey-white rectangular equipment block with a darker top, a brown strip and a small green potted plant on its right side, bare floor around it

purpose: the ruined shell of a large crew quarters, wrecked and unusable; the former sleeping halls lie in ruins, burnt out and covered in debris.
what: a wrecked quarters hall, one large open ruined hall: a dark reddish-brown scorched floor, faint grey outlines of broken low bunk partitions and cabinets in a grid pattern, many round black blast holes and craters with rusty orange rims scattered across the floor, rubble and soot, a lighter broken wall edge at the top

purpose: the damaged remains of a luxury condo, once a comfortable high-class residence with a pool; now battered by an attack and only partly usable.
what: a battered luxury condo, one large open hall (no inner walls): a beige and tan floor with orange tiled walkways, a long vertical blue water pool in the middle bordered by green hedges on both sides, white and grey furniture blocks, beds and counters along the left and right sides, large black craters with dark purple rims scattered over the floor, a small blue object at the bottom

purpose: the revolution headquarters, the heart of the whole revolutionary effort: a huge barracks and command complex where the crew lives, trains, plans, builds weapons and treats wounds.
what: a huge fortified headquarters, one large open hall: thick grey riveted steel armour plating forming wide bands along the top, the left side and the right side with black-yellow hazard stripes on their inner edges, inside a brown rocky earth floor with a big pale grey concrete slab in the middle-left with painted rectangle outlines, clusters of blue and purple bunks and lockers along the left, right and bottom edges, a red grated square hatch in the bottom left corner, a small red banner mark in the top left, a grey hatch block at the top right

purpose: the ruins of a vault storeroom, wrecked and empty of useful goods; only debris remains where guns and loot were once kept.
what: a ruined storeroom on a dark brown floor inside a dark metal frame: a heap of rusty round barrels and crushed crates in the middle and upper part, scattered scrap and debris, black burnt patches

purpose: an armored vault where wares are stored under heavy protection, with its own anti-aircraft gun mount and a small workbench for the crew.
what: an armored storeroom with a purple-grey floor: stacks of orange-brown crates in the middle and on the right, an octagonal grey armoured ring wall around the central stack with a dark red gun mount inside it, a green gun turret in the top left corner, a patch of green foliage at the bottom left

purpose: a compact prison where captives are kept frozen in stasis pods; they sleep in the cold with no need for food, guards or cells.
what: a cryogenic prison on a purple-grey metal floor: two rows of three upright pale-blue glass stasis pods, one row along the top and one along the bottom, cables and pipes running between them, a small red marker lamp in the middle-left and a blue lamp on the left wall

purpose: the Eye of Horus, an ultimate detection facility built with advanced physics and shadow arts that sees every ship and hideout on the planet.
what: an octagonal chamber with a violet-purple floor: four big grey-brown domed machines in the corners and in the middle a huge watching eye with a green iris, a black vertical slit pupil and a glowing orange-red eyelid ring

purpose: the wrecked remains of a hangar where an aircraft used to land; the landing bay is damaged and cannot hold a craft.
what: a wrecked landing bay, one huge open hall (no inner walls) with the middle kept free: a very dark brown-black scorched floor, a large circular landing pad outline in the middle with faded arrow markings pointing left and right and a few light crosses, a ring of black blast craters with rusty orange rims around the pad, diagonal debris and broken plating in the top right corner, lighter stripes and wreckage at the bottom

purpose: an anti-aircraft battery of flak cannons that fends off weaker enemy ships attacking the hideout, plus a gun emplacement that helps in ground fights when the hideout is invaded.
what: a flak defense battery in a cross-shaped room: a pale beige-khaki floor, a green round spherical flak turret in the middle with a long dark green barrel pointing up, on a green four-pointed mount

purpose: the armory tower, a fortified weapons tower that guards the hideout with defensive fire, stores arms and gives the crew a place to assemble unique military hardware.
what: an armory tower on a dark grey steel floor: in the middle a large square thick grey frame with a grid of blue glass tiles (a hatch), white round turret domes in the corners of the room, small red lamps and bolts along the edges, a blue lamp on the left wall

purpose: a club where the crew's master lures rich VIPs and prizefighting hopefuls with drinks, hot baths, fights and fun; a private office above watches over the crowd, and the crew can use it for training in the daytime.
what: a VIP club on a dark maroon carpeted floor: a black L-shaped bar counter running along the top and left, a green felt gaming table in the lower right, rows of small round orange-gold lamps along the top and left walls

purpose: a comfortable hotel with food, gambling and culture for guests, run by the crew; it has its own large hot spring and holds guests, crew and their belongings.
what: a hotel, one large open hall with grey blocks: a dark steel mesh floor, a wide light grey reception and lounge block in the top left with a dark slot and three small diamond lamps at its right, a narrow grey block with a pale oval below it on the left, a glass-walled hot spring pool with blue water and white steam in the lower right with a grey frame and pipes, a red dotted carpet rug in the bottom left corner

purpose: a garden of highly mutated plants grown on hellerium sludge: they give power, heal the crew, feed the neighbouring shantytown and a special tree even senses enemies; the undergrowth is hard to walk through.
what: a mutant garden with a lush green jungle floor: thick dark and bright green plants over the whole room, a cream-white curved pipe or path winding diagonally from the upper left to the right, a small blue puddle at the bottom, brown rocks on the right

purpose: a trap corridor that looks like a normal passage; firebombs hidden in the walls blow when intruders walk in and make them stop and burn.
what: a cross-shaped trap corridor: a red perforated steel floor plate with a regular grid of small dark red dots, pale tan metal walls around the cross edge

purpose: a plantation where automated lighting and watering grow valuable sectoweed in stages from planting to harvest; the crew tends the plants and harvests them.
what: a hydroponic plantation, one large open hall (no inner walls): four square beds of dark brown soil with straight vertical rows of small green plants, a thick lavender-purple cross-shaped water pipe running through the middle both ways with round grey valve bolts at the centre and at its four arms, grey outer border

purpose: an apiary where uberbees gather nectar from the plantations and make uberhoney that the crew sells; tunnels link the hive to the farm, and the bees attack strangers who disturb them.
what: a bee hive room with a pale yellow honeycomb dotted floor: dark brown honeycomb cell rows across the top, two rows of small dark cell holes in the upper and middle part, a strip of green moss at the bottom right

purpose: a chemical refinery that makes chemicals and advanced chemical weapons, with workspace for workers and a bench for a researcher.
what: a chemical refinery on a dark grey floor: a large round ribbed grey-violet tank at the top, a big beige-grey curved pipe body on the left, orange pipes at the top left, a few green spilled drops and a small round grey gauge at the bottom right

purpose: a huge factory, the industrial centre of the hideout, where hundreds of workers turn out equipment on production lines at lower running cost.
what: an industrial factory, one large open hall on a dark grey steel floor: long dark ribbed conveyor lines with orange rungs, two running vertically near the top centre and right edge, two long ones running horizontally across the middle and the bottom, small lavender press machines and pipe sections along the lines, a small black-walled machine bay in the top left corner with an orange machine inside, black wall segments along the top and left sides

purpose: a luxury library with books of every kind, paper, crystal and electronic, romance, adventure and even arcane works; a place for a scholar to work and required for fancy research.
what: a library on a soft pink-lavender floor: three long rows of dark grey bookshelves stacked in horizontal rows across the room, a small lavender writing desk at the top left

purpose: a data centre where powerful central computers crunch huge amounts of data and several brainers work, linked into a network with the lab.
what: a data centre on a pinkish-beige floor: two small green-topped units on the left, a lavender-blue console block in the middle top, a grey kiosk at the top right, two white server cabinets with blue panels along the right edge

purpose: a showpiece laboratory that earns grant money: a glossy, high-tech lab with interns, merchandise and a big glowing ball of wow in the middle that dazzles the governments.
what: an octagonal showpiece lab with a pale speckled beige outer rim and a grey floor: in the middle a square pedestal with a glowing green ball, four yellow-orange-green striped lines running from it up, down, left and right to the walls, a small red lamp at the top

purpose: the remains of a ruined facility that keep a way open for people and pipes; it is unprotected and can be cleared to make a burrow.
what: a heap of dark rubble filling the whole room: dark grey and black broken stones and concrete chunks, twisted pipes and round pipe ends, small green patches at the left and top left edges, this cell has NO outer wall and no frame: the rubble fills it edge to edge, ignore the instruction to keep an outer wall

purpose: a plasma battery: powerful plasma beam cannons that shoot at hostile craft, with a turreted plasma cannon inside to sweep the corridors if enemies get in; it needs its own power station.
what: a plasma defense battery in a cross-shaped (plus-sign) room: a smooth tan sandy-beige floor, in the middle a round blue-steel plasma turret with a glowing violet-blue spherical core on a four-pointed blue mount, a small green-yellow beacon lamp at the top of the turret, cables and a few small crates only along the walls

purpose: a voodoo school where the crew's magical aptitude is assessed and trained, and students learn sorcery and defence against enemy dark arts.
what: a voodoo school on a warm orange-brown wooden plank floor: on the left a tall dark-red lacquered cabinet or bookshelf along the wall, on the right two dark-red ritual desks one above the other, each with a pale grey-white crystal skull or orb on it, a few scrolls and candles by the walls

purpose: living capsules: personnel sleep stacked in drawer-like sleeping pods, an efficient but cramped way to house a crew.
what: a capsule dormitory on a dark brown-grey metal floor: four long rounded grey sleeping capsules with small dark windows and tiny red indicator lights, arranged in rows (two stacked on top and two below, offset), a narrow aisle between them, a purple cable or bag in the left edge

purpose: luxury quarters: a sealed, comfortable modern living block for fifty people with good beds and creature comforts, topped with a defensive laser cannon and a tracking radar.
what: a sealed high-tech residential block packed with grey-blue machinery panels: pale grey and lilac metal floor plates, a white round radar dish at the top left with two small red lamps beside it, an orange-brown patterned carpet or rug area in the middle, grey consoles and cylindrical units along the bottom and the right edge, cables and pipes

purpose: a bunker: a heavily armoured defensive building leaving only a narrow road through the main level, blocked by a remote-controlled turret; it also houses some crew and storage.
what: a heavily armoured concrete bunker seen from above: a uniform light grey riveted steel-concrete roof plate filling the whole cell with a bevelled raised edge, four small X-shaped hatch marks (or bolt crosses) near the four corners, a row of dark bolts along the bottom edge, nothing else

purpose: the lightly damaged headquarters of a revolution: a former barracks and command hall of a rebel force, scarred by fighting but still usable as a base.
what: a war-damaged barracks hall, one large open hall (no inner walls) in a 3x3 square: dark grey riveted steel wall-blocks and bulkheads along the top, the left side and the bottom-right edge; the middle is an open reddish-brown dirt and rubble floor with a lighter grey concrete floor island in the centre holding a faint pale rectangular outline; small purple and blue crates, bedrolls and bunks along the edges of the dirt area; around ten scorched round blast craters with dark charred rims scattered over the floor, a tattered red flag with a dark emblem at the top left, a red grated hatch panel in the bottom left corner, a small grey ramp or stairs at the right of the middle, a white-grey corner pad at the top right

purpose: large vaults: huge storage halls that hold far more loot, guns and junk than the ordinary vaults and also have space for a workshop.
what: a large storage complex, one large open hall (no inner walls) on a dark grey asphalt-like concrete floor crossed by lanes: it is divided into separate walled-off pale grey storage bays like a city block, each filled with goods: stacked grey-lilac boulders or rock crates at the left, rows of green bushes or plants in boxes at the top, orange-brown crates and barrels in the middle bay, red and pink containers at the right, green plants at the bottom, a blue item at the top left; the wide dark lanes between the bays are kept free

purpose: damaged armoured vaults: a found storage facility for wares and loot, strong but broken - its anti-aircraft gun no longer works.
what: a damaged armoured storage vault, a cluttered pile: a dark grey metal floor under many heavy round dark-grey gun-barrel mounts and cylinders in the corners and the middle (broken anti-aircraft gun parts), orange-brown crates and a pile of rubble in the middle with a dark pit, a green plant patch at the top left, a small blue item at the bottom left, white-grey boxes

purpose: a dungeon: a cheap high-security prison for a few hostages with a fun room where captives are broken into obedient slaves.
what: a grim dungeon cell block on a reddish brown rough stone floor: the whole floor is one big carved stone face, two grey metal-grated eyes and a nose with a mouth of horizontal stone steps in the middle, dark brown stone walls, iron bars and chains by the walls, nothing else

purpose: a space communications centre: a device that lets the hideout talk to distant planets and governments and listen to entertainment broadcasts from outer worlds.
what: a space communications room, an octagonal room with a pale lilac-grey metal floor: two violet-blue radio consoles with glowing screens and keypads (one at the top right, one at the bottom left, tilted), a blue-and-orange equipment rack at the top left, a small green and orange antenna or plant at the left edge, cables across the floor

purpose: an irradiator tower: a radar dish that glows white-hot when fuelled by hellerium sludge turbines, hurting enemy attackers and serving as a radar, at the cost of heavy radiation.
